boundaries.statement: Admission of a proposal is not evidence that the provider computed anything. The witness is compared to the core's OWN sealed import and acceptance terminates in the core re-evaluating the contract over all Boolean prestates, so a provider that merely echoes the correct record is admitted. This is by design for this capability - the provider is untrusted and contributes no authority - and is not a soundness gap, but it means no Safe result here may be attributed to provider analysis.

BooleanFieldSourceTask::check returns the whole coverage set of the task it validated. That is sound only because its own derivation emits exactly one obligation and it refuses every task it did not derive. Row 5.1 pins both halves; a future multi-obligation derivation for this capability must change check to attribute per obligation.

The witness schema carries no import identity of its own (BooleanSourceIdentity is serde(skip)). Two imports whose schema records are byte-identical therefore have interchangeable witness RECORDS; only the outer core-computed task digest separates them. Rows 2.7-2.9 pin that this outer binding is load-bearing.

Every row is scoped to the ChunkIO Boolean-field capability (qcore.c_boolean_field_contract.v2). The CMetrics unit-result capability (v3), chunk lifecycle and observation replay each need their own matrix; none is claimed here.

E01-B1 is unchanged and still open: a definition visible only after macro expansion, or a K&R-style definition, is absent from the raw function enumeration and therefore from the derived inventory. No mutation row repairs it; it never promotes anything.
